findings.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:483 — isAccessTokenId's grant-shortcut check uses wrong substring offset (3,5) instead of the real field position (4,6) AND inverts the boolean (returns false on match, falls through to true on non-match), so for every real grant shortcut (ac/rt/dg/ci) the check can never accidentally align, making the grant-type assertion dead code that always passes as long as items[0].length==6 and the UUID part matches - traced concretely: "onrtac:1234" (wrong grant "ac" encoded) vs isAccessTokenId("rt") still returns true because substring(3,5)="ta" != "rt" so it falls through to isUUID() which is true; this is a true silent-pass gate that would let every integration test asserting a grant-type-encoded token ID pass in CI regardless of whether TokenManager/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider actually encodes the correct grant shortcut

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:47 — getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext calls clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession() with no null-check on getClientSession()/getUserSession(); likely non-null by construction elsewhere in the codebase but not defensively verified here, so any future/edge caller that reaches this with an incomplete ClientSessionContext will NPE instead of failing gracefully

goldens.comment: In AccessTokenContext constructor, the fourth Objects.requireNonNull validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId values to pass validation.

In isAccessTokenId, the substring for the grant shortcut and the equality check look inverted: the grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5 (substring(4,6)), and a match should return true (combined with UUID check), not false.

Javadoc mentions "usually like 3-letters shortcut" but some implementations use 2-letter shortcuts ("ac", "cc", "rt", "te", "pc", "ci", "ro"). Consider updating documentation to reflect actual usage pattern.
Catching generic RuntimeException is too broad. The implementation throws IllegalArgumentException specifically - catch that instead for more precise testing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/TokenManager.java:1050 — initToken now unconditionally encodes access token `id`/`jti` as `<6-char-context>:<uuid>` (was plain UUID via generateId()) with no config toggle/legacy-format opt-out, breaking any external consumer (introspection clients, SIEM/log parsers, custom DB columns) that validates/stores the token id as a UUID

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `TokenManager.initToken(...)` no longer sets `token.id(generateId())`; instead it always obtains a `TokenContextEncoderProvider` and sets `token.id(encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx))`, producing a prefixed format (`<6 chars>:<rawTokenId>`) via `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(...)`. The diff also registers the default provider SPI (`TokenContextEncoderSpi` + `META-INF/services/...TokenContextEncoderProviderFactory`), and there is no conditional/config flag in the shown changes to preserve the legacy plain-UUID token id format. While `jti` being non-UUID isn’t inherently incorrect (it’s a string), this is a concrete backward-compatibility/consumer-impact concern grounded in the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:102 — Removal of `Context(Context context)` copy constructor is unrelated scope creep in an encoding-feature PR, though verified dead (zero callers repo-wide) so not a behavioral break

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `Context(Context context)` copy constructor, but it’s not verifiable from the diff that it is “unrelated scope creep” or “verified dead (zero callers repo-wide)”. Also, given the newly added `grantType` field initialized from `formParams`, keeping a copy constructor without updating it to copy/derive `grantType` could be problematic; removing it can be directly related to the new grantType/context-encoding changes rather than unrelated refactoring.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/ClientCredentialsGrantTypeFactory.java:40 — Inconsistent pattern across the ~9 grant type factories: AuthorizationCodeGrantTypeFactory, RefreshTokenGrantTypeFactory, CibaGrantTypeFactory, DeviceGrantTypeFactory expose a `public static final String GRANT_SHORTCUT` constant while ClientCredentials/Permission/PreAuthorizedCode/ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentials/TokenExchange factories inline the same 2-char literal directly in getShortcut()

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show an inconsistency: some grant factories define a `public static final String GRANT_SHORTCUT` (e.g., `AuthorizationCodeGrantTypeFactory`, `RefreshTokenGrantTypeFactory`, `CibaGrantTypeFactory`, `DeviceGrantTypeFactory`) while others return a 2-char literal directly in `getShortcut()` (e.g., `ClientCredentialsGrantTypeFactory` returns "cc", `PermissionGrantTypeFactory` returns "pg", etc.). However, this is a stylistic/consistency nit with no verifiable functional impact in the diff (all implementations still satisfy the new `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` contract).

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:47 — getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext calls clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession() with no null-check on getClientSession()/getUserSession(); likely non-null by construction elsewhere in the codebase but not defensively verified here, so any future/edge caller that reaches this with an incomplete ClientSessionContext will NPE instead of failing gracefully

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider#getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext, the code immediately dereferences clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession() without guarding against either being null. The diff does not prove these can be null in current call sites (e.g., TokenManager.initToken passes a ClientSessionContext that is likely fully populated), so it’s not a verifiable defect, but it is a concrete robustness/edge-case concern introduced by this new API surface: a partially constructed/alternate ClientSessionContext would NPE rather than yielding UNKNOWN session type or a clearer error.
